thread.title: Big Week Ahead For U.S. Stocks

author: Nasdaq
title: Big Week Ahead For U.S. Stocks
text:
Shutterstock photo Monday, January 29, 2018, 11:00 AM, EST NASDAQ Composite -0.5% Dow -0.48% S&P 500 -0.50% Russell 2000 -0.32% S&P MID 400 -0.56% NASDAQ Advancers: 845 Decliners: 1411 Today's Volume (100 day avg) +11% US equities are under slight pressure this morning, possible taking a breather ahead of more than 100 S&P 500 companies reporting results, and Janet Yellen's last FOMC meeting. All S&P sectors are lower, as the Utility, Telecom, and Real Estate Indices all off by more than 1%. The Beverage & Staple industry saw a large deal hit the tape this morning this morning. Energy and Metal related commodities are lower today.
Janet Yellen's position as the Fed Chairman is coming to an end, leading the way for a committee led by Jerome Powell. The theme behind this week's meeting will be transitioning leadership while the US economy looks to be gearing up for growth. A gradual approach to raising rates in a fragile market will likely be what Yellen is remembered for, despite inflation falling short of expectations, held down by lackluster wage growth. Powell is stepping into the role with equities trading at all-time highs, historic low unemployment, while leading US politicians apparently are showing less support for the US Dollar. Godspeed Jerome… Merger Monday: There were three notable merger announcements this morning. Dr. Pepper Snapple rose 37% this morning, pre-opening, after it announced it would merge with Keurig Green Mountain creating a new soft-drink & coffee behemoth controlled by JAB Holdings. As a result of this deal, Mondelez International ( MDLZ ) who owns 24% of Keurig will own approximately 13.5% of the new company. KapStone Paper and Packaging rose 32% after it announced it will be acquired by WestRock ( WRK ) for $35/share, while Sanofo will buy ABlynx, ( ABLX ) for EUR45 per share in cash. ABLX rose 14% this morning in early trading. YTD we have seen $356.6 billion of announced or proposed deals globally. Four of the Five FAANG stocks will report earnings this week and will have a tough time replicating the price action of the "N", Netflix, which reported results and subscriber growth that saw shares shoot up by 25% last week. FB (1/31), AMZN (2/1), AAPL (2/1) and GOOG (2/1), will all post results after the close on their earnings dates. Retail stocks saw a strong finish to 2017. Holiday spending to end the year was strong and shows signs of continuation in 2018. According to Telsey Advisory Group ( TAG ), specialty retail should continue to grow in 2018. "First, we believe that momentum from a strong holiday season in 2017 can continue into 2018. The important holiday selling season has shown to be a directional indicator for the first half of the following year in our group. In addition, FY18 also benefits from particularly benign compares against the first half of last year. Despite the strong run that our stocks have seen since bottoming in August last year, valuations remain fairly reasonable relative to historical averages. Moreover, we believe multiples stand to become more attractive as earnings estimates climb from tax reform benefits." Consumer spend is an important factor in U.S. GDP and any signs of strength there should be viewed as a positive for the economy. Technical Take: Bunds on the Breakout
Financials are one of the few groups in the green today due in part to rising rates where the 10-Year treasury Yield has lifted to 2.73%, its highest level since May 2014. Now with a "melt-up" in equities underway, there is increasing chatter the Fed could add an additional rate hike in 2018 on top of the three hikes already expected. Another factor pushing US yields higher is the price action in the global bond markets. Specifically the 10-Year German Bund Yield has made a significant move the last two sessions first by closing above the 0.62% resistance on Friday, and then today gapping higher and running to 0.69%. The long German yield is now making a two year high and more importantly it is breaking above a ten-year downtrend line. Also noteworthy is the weekly RSI, now 58, which has broken above a seven year resistance level at 56. With both price and momentum breaking out above major multi-yr resistance levels, the ensuing move could be stronger and last far longer than what many would otherwise expect. This scenario should put upward pressure on sovereign yields across the globe. The pace of the rise in yields is most important and could determine whether or not equities continue to react favorably, or if they get spooked by potentially violent price action in global bond markets.
